title: Être et avoir : identité, état, âge et possession
summary: Give an identity, a state, an age and a possession using two essential present-tense verbs.
objectives: Recall all present forms of être and avoir.
Distinguish being from having, including French age expressions.

sections.title: Être connects the subject to an identity or state
paragraphs: Être means to be. Its present forms are irregular: learn the whole set rather than adding regular endings. Il, elle and on share one form; ils and elles share another. With a bare profession after être, French normally omits the English a/an: elle est médecin. Un médecin (m.) is a doctor; the profession can describe a woman too.
The present can describe what is true now or generally. A describing word, called an adjective, can change with the subject: prêt for masculine singular, prête for feminine singular.
points: Être describes who someone is, how they are or where they are.
Keep the accents in êtes and the infinitive être.

examples.french:
Je **suis**
Tu **es**
Il/elle/on **est**
Nous **sommes**
Vous **êtes**
Ils/elles **sont**
examples.english:
I am
You are
He/she is; one is/we are
We are
You are
They are
examples.note: The full present paradigm; on keeps est even when it means we.
A bare profession follows être without an indefinite article.
The adjective is masculine plural for this group.
Polite singular vous keeps the plural verb but the adjective describes one woman.

mistakes.why: Nous requires sommes, not the ils/elles form.

sections.title: Avoir expresses possession, age and several familiar feelings
paragraphs: Avoir means to have. It also expresses age: avoir + number + ans, literally to have a number of years. Un an (m.) is a year. French uses avoir, not être, in avoir faim (be hungry), avoir soif (be thirsty), avoir chaud (feel hot) and avoir froid (feel cold). These fixed expressions need no article before faim, soif, chaud or froid.
J'ai has an apostrophe because je meets a vowel. In il a, a has no accent; à with an accent is a different word, a preposition meaning at or to.
points: Avoir: j'ai, tu as, il/elle/on a, nous avons, vous avez, ils/elles ont.
Être and avoir do not translate every English use word for word.

examples.french:
J'**ai**
Tu **as**
Il/elle/on **a**
Nous **avons**
Vous **avez**
Ils/elles **ont**
examples.english:
I have
You have
He/she/one has; we have
We have
You have
They have
examples.note: Each subject needs its own form.
This is a person's sensation, not a weather report.
Rising intonation turns the statement order into a question.

mistakes.why: Ils takes ont; avons belongs to nous.

practice.prompt: Supply être in the present: 'Je ___ à Lyon.'

practice.explanation: Vous requires êtes, including polite singular vous.
Les portes is a plural subject equivalent to elles.
On always takes the third-person singular verb.
Nous avons is the first-person plural.

practice.prompt: Write je + avoir in the present, with the required apostrophe.
You want water. Choose the ordinary expression.
practice.explanation: Avoir soif means to be thirsty.

practice.prompt: Supply être: 'Toi et moi, nous ___ prêts.'

practice.explanation: Avez is the vous form; hunger uses avoir.
Tu takes es; the bare profession needs no article.

practice.prompt: Rewrite the whole sentence, changing only the verb: 'Elle est dix-neuf ans.'

practice.explanation: On takes a in the sensation expression avoir froid.

practice.prompt: A woman is being addressed politely. Choose the correct sentence.
practice.explanation: Polite singular vous still requires êtes.

production_task.prompt: Write a short introduction for a new class: give your name with Je suis, your age with avoir and something you have. You may invent the details.
production_task.model_answer: Je suis Nora. J'ai vingt-huit ans. J'ai un vélo.
production_task.translation: I am Nora. I am twenty-eight years old. I have a bicycle.
rubric: Use suis for identity and ai for age and possession.
Include an article with the possessed countable object.
